question: A conductor of length $L$ has a non-uniform cross-section and tapers uniformly such that its radius increases linearly from $r$ at one end (narrow end) to $2r$ at the other end. It carries a steady current $I$ along its length. If the charge carrier density $n$ is constant throughout, what is the ratio of drift velocity at the narrow end to the drift velocity at the midpoint (at $x=\frac{L}{2}$) of the conductor?
